newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia farmers say drought of economic concern.
newsitem.headline: Australia farmers say drought of economic concern.

text.p: Australia's deteriorating drought outlook was a serious worry because of potential loss of export income and its effect on job growth, New South Wales Farmers Association chief executive Peter Comensoli said on Wednesday.

Most crops were in the ground in the hope of further rain to build soil moisture to the necessary level for harvest, he said in a statement. He was commenting on a Bureau of Meteorology report which warned that large areas of eastern Australia were likely to be significantly drier than normal during the southern hemisphere winter and spring due to an El Nino weather pattern and negative Southern Oscillation Index.
Last year there were similar dire predictions but rain came in the right places at the right time for the grain industry to enjoy a record crop in NSW, Comensoli said.

"There are several pockets in NSW where there has been no rain, so crops are yet to be planted and pastures are suffering," he said. "There is also the risk that even if rain does fall now, it is too late in many parts of the state to promote the growth of grasses needed to feed livestock."
El Nino is based on sea surface tempoeratures and the Southern Oscillation Index on air pressure readings.
